library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno"))$reference`
* Article: [Pharmacol Res Perspect 2015;3(1):e00098](https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.98)
  (open access)

Abrilumab (AMG 181, MEDI7183) is a human IgG2 monoclonal antibody against the
alpha4beta7 integrin on gut-homing T cells. Li 2015 fits a two-compartment
target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model with the quasi-equilibrium (QE)
approximation to serum abrilumab from five cynomolgus monkey studies, relates
free alpha4beta7 on CD4+ T cells to concentration with an inhibitory Emax
model, and scales the monkey PK allometrically to humans to choose the
first-in-human (FIH) doses. The paper contributes two models:

| Model | Species | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno` | cynomolgus monkey | fitted TMDD-QE PK with IIV and residual error; Emax PD of free alpha4beta7 | Table 2; Results text |
| `Li_2015_abrilumab_human` | human (projection) | typical-value TMDD-QE PK scaled from the monkey | Table 3; Methods |

Both models take doses in mg and report `Cc`, the **free** abrilumab
concentration, in nmol/L (molecular weight about 144 kDa, so 1 nmol/L =
0.144 ug/mL). The paper fitted molar concentrations with the free
concentration computed by the QE equation of Figure 1, and its human
predictions (Table 4) are reproduced by the free concentration only (shown
below).

# Population

* **Monkey** (`Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno`). 119 actively treated cynomolgus
  monkeys (73 male, 46 female; 86 SC, 33 IV) from two single-dose PK/PD
  studies (A, C), a two-dose non-GLP toxicology study (B) and 3- and 6-month
  GLP toxicology studies (D, E), dosed at 0.01-80 mg/kg (Table 1). Body
  weight 2.1-6.4 kg, median 2.8 kg. Anti-drug antibodies were common except
  at 80 mg/kg; 120 of 1743 ADA-affected concentrations were excluded. The PD
  model used Study A only.
* **Human** (`Li_2015_abrilumab_human`). No human data were fitted. The
  monkey model was scaled to a 70 kg adult and compared afterwards with the
  FIH study (7 mg SC to 420 mg IV; Figure 7).

The same information is in the `population` element of each model, e.g.
`readModelDb("Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2-compartment TMDD, QE approximation, SC first-order absorption | -- | Methods 'PK structural models'; Figure 1 |
| Free drug `Cf = 0.5 * ((Ctot - Rtot - Kd) + sqrt((Ctot - Rtot - Kd)^2 + 4 Kd Ctot))` | -- | Figure 1 |
| KA (both species) | 0.846 /day | Table 2; Table 3 |
| CL monkey / human | 12.9 / 144 mL/day | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| Vc monkey / human | 116 / 2900 mL | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| K12 monkey / human | 0.617 / 0.276 /day | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| K21 monkey / human | 0.877 / 0.392 /day | Table 2 / Table 3 |
| Kd monkey (fixed) | 0.013 nmol/L | Table 2; Methods |
| Kd human (fixed) | 0.031 nmol/L | Methods 'Allometric scaling and simulation of human PK' (Table 3 prints 0.013; see below) |
| Rtot (both species) | 9.18 nmol/L | Table 2; Table 3 |
| Kint (both species) | 0.0215 /day | Table 2; Table 3 |
| F1 (fixed) | 1 | Results text; Table 3 |
| IIV CL, Vc, correlation | 44.1%, 46.1%, 0.642 | Table 2 |
| IIV Rtot | 180% | Table 2 |
| Proportional / additive residual error | 20.1% / 1.11 nmol/L | Table 2 |
| PD: `E = E0 * (1 - Emax * C / (EC50 + C))` | -- | Methods equation |
| E0, Emax, EC50 | 531 MFI, 0.922, 0.0140 ug/mL | Results 'Modeling of AMG 181 PD in cynomolgus monkeys' |
| Allometric exponents CL 0.75, Vc 1, K12/K21 -0.25; 2.8 kg monkey to 70 kg human | -- | Methods |
| Molecular weight | about 144 kDa | Methods 'In vitro pharmacology studies' |

```{r models}
mod_cyno <- readModelDb("Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno")
mod_human <- readModelDb("Li_2015_abrilumab_human")
mw_factor <- 0.144 # ug/mL per nmol/L

# PKNCA Cmax and AUC over one interval of a simulated profile; time in days
# is converted to hours so AUC is in h*ug/mL as in the paper.
nca_interval <- function(sim, group, doses, start, end, auc = "aucinf.obs") {
  conc <- sim |>
    transmute(id, grp = .data[[group]], time_h = time * 24, conc = conc_ug)
  dose <- doses |>
    transmute(id, grp = .data[[group]], time_h = time * 24, dose = amt)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = start * 24, end = end * 24, cmax = TRUE)
  intervals[[auc]] <- TRUE
  o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time_h | grp + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, dose ~ time_h | grp + id),
    intervals = intervals
  )
  as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)) |>
    select(grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
}
```

# Allometric scaling reproduces Table 3

The human values in Table 3 follow from Table 2 and the stated exponents.

```{r scaling}
ratio <- 70 / 2.8
scaling <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("CL (mL/day)", "Vc (mL)", "K12 (1/day)", "K21 (1/day)"),
  monkey = c(12.9, 116, 0.617, 0.877),
  exponent = c(0.75, 1, -0.25, -0.25),
  table3 = c(144, 2900, 0.276, 0.392)
) |>
  mutate(scaled = monkey * ratio^exponent, pct_diff = 100 * (scaled - table3) / table3)
stopifnot(all(abs(scaling$pct_diff) < 0.5))
scaling |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Monkey (Table 2)" = monkey, "Exponent" = exponent,
    "Table 3 human" = table3, "Scaled" = scaled, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Monkey model

## Typical single- and multiple-dose profiles (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the mean of individual predictions per cohort. Below are the
typical-value profiles for a 2.8 kg (median-weight) monkey; doses in mg/kg
are converted with that weight. Because Rtot carries a large IIV, the
typical curve sits below the mean of individual predictions at the lowest
doses, where target binding dominates.

```{r cyno-fig2}
wt_monkey <- 2.8
cohorts_single <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~mgkg, ~cmt,
  "0.01 mg/kg IV", 0.01, "central",
  "0.1 mg/kg IV", 0.1, "central",
  "1 mg/kg IV", 1, "central",
  "3 mg/kg IV", 3, "central",
  "3 mg/kg SC", 3, "depot",
  "9 mg/kg IV", 9, "central",
  "9 mg/kg SC", 9, "depot"
)
cohorts_multi <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~mgkg, ~cmt, ~ndose,
  "0.5 mg/kg SC QW x 2", 0.5, "depot", 2,
  "80 mg/kg SC QW x 2", 80, "depot", 2,
  "5 mg/kg SC QW x 13", 5, "depot", 13,
  "20 mg/kg SC QW x 13", 20, "depot", 13,
  "80 mg/kg SC QW x 13", 80, "depot", 13,
  "80 mg/kg IV QW x 13", 80, "central", 13,
  "20 mg/kg SC QW x 24", 20, "depot", 24,
  "80 mg/kg SC QW x 24", 80, "depot", 24
)

make_events <- function(id, cohort, dose_mg, cmt, ndose, obs_times) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, cohort = cohort, time = 7 * (seq_len(ndose) - 1), amt = dose_mg,
    evid = 1L, cmt = cmt
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, cohort = cohort, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  rbind(doses, obs)
}

ev_single <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts_single)), function(i) {
  make_events(i, cohorts_single$cohort[i], cohorts_single$mgkg[i] * wt_monkey,
    cohorts_single$cmt[i], 1, c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 28, by = 0.25)))
}))
ev_multi <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts_multi)), function(i) {
  make_events(100 + i, cohorts_multi$cohort[i], cohorts_multi$mgkg[i] * wt_monkey,
    cohorts_multi$cmt[i], cohorts_multi$ndose[i], seq(0, 364, by = 0.5))
}))

# zeroRe() removes the omega matrix, so rxode2 warns that a multi-subject
# solve has no omega; the typical-value solve is what is wanted here.
sim_cyno_typ <- function(ev) {
  suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_cyno), events = ev, keep = "cohort",
    returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)) |>
    mutate(conc_ug = Cc * mw_factor)
}
typ_single <- sim_cyno_typ(ev_single)
typ_multi <- sim_cyno_typ(ev_multi)

ggplot(typ_single |> filter(time > 0, conc_ug >= 1e-4), aes(time, conc_ug, colour = cohort)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 2A of Li 2015 (typical 2.8 kg monkey)")

ggplot(typ_multi |> filter(time > 0, conc_ug >= 1e-4), aes(time, conc_ug, colour = cohort)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time post first dose (days)", y = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 2B of Li 2015 (typical 2.8 kg monkey)")
```

## Visual predictive check (Figure 4)

The 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of 100 simulated monkeys per cohort,
with IIV and residual error, for three cohorts spanning the dose range.

```{r cyno-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20150101)
n_vpc <- 100
vpc_cohorts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~mgkg, ~cmt, ~ndose,
  "0.1 mg/kg IV", 0.1, "central", 1,
  "9 mg/kg SC", 9, "depot", 1,
  "80 mg/kg SC QW x 13", 80, "depot", 13
)
ev_vpc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(vpc_cohorts)), function(i) {
  obs_t <- if (vpc_cohorts$ndose[i] == 1) c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 21, 28) else seq(0, 280, by = 7)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_vpc), function(j) {
    make_events(1000 * i + j, vpc_cohorts$cohort[i], vpc_cohorts$mgkg[i] * wt_monkey,
      vpc_cohorts$cmt[i], vpc_cohorts$ndose[i], obs_t)
  }))
}))
vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cyno, events = ev_vpc, keep = "cohort", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(conc_ug = sim * mw_factor) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(cohort, time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(conc_ug, 0.1), p50 = median(conc_ug), p90 = quantile(conc_ug, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(p10, 1e-4), ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~cohort, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)",
    title = "Simulated 10th-50th-90th percentiles (cf. Figure 4 of Li 2015)")
```

The additive residual error (1.11 nmol/L = 0.16 ug/mL) makes the lower
percentile negative at the lowest concentrations, as in any additive-error
simulation; the ribbon is floored for the log axis.

## Half-lives stated in the text

The text gives a linear elimination half-life of about 12 days and a
receptor-internalization half-life of about 32 days (0.693 / Kint).

```{r cyno-halflife}
kel <- 12.9 / 116
k12 <- 0.617
k21 <- 0.877
beta <- ((kel + k12 + k21) - sqrt((kel + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2
t_half_beta <- log(2) / beta
t_half_kint <- log(2) / 0.0215
c(linear_terminal_half_life_day = t_half_beta, kint_half_life_day = t_half_kint)
stopifnot(abs(t_half_kint - 32) < 0.5, abs(t_half_beta - 12) < 1.5)
```

The terminal half-life of the linear two-compartment part is
`r round(t_half_beta, 1)` days against the stated "12 days"; the paper does
not say how its figure was computed.

## NOAEL exposure (Methods, 'Exposure margins')

The observed Cmax and AUC at the 80 mg/kg IV QW NOAEL in Study D were
4850 ug/mL and 485,000 h*ug/mL. The paper does not state the dosing
interval to which these refer; the model values for the last (13th) weekly
interval of a typical 2.8 kg monkey are shown for orientation only. They are
somewhat lower than observed, in line with the paper's remark that the model
had to reconcile higher SC than IV exposure at 80 mg/kg.

```{r cyno-noael}
noael_sim <- typ_multi |>
  filter(cohort == "80 mg/kg IV QW x 13")
noael_dose <- ev_multi |>
  filter(evid == 1, cohort == "80 mg/kg IV QW x 13")
nca_interval(noael_sim, "cohort", noael_dose, start = 84, end = 91, auc = "auclast") |>
  dplyr::rename("Cohort" = grp, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "AUC day 84-91 (h*ug/mL)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)
```

## Free alpha4beta7 Emax model (Figure 5)

The PD model is the algebraic output `mfi_a4b7` of `Li_2015_abrilumab_cyno`.
The text derives EC75, EC90 and EC99 of 0.042, 0.126 and 1.38 ug/mL from it;
for this model ECx = EC50 * x / (100 - x).

```{r cyno-pd}
ec50 <- 0.0140
ecx <- c(EC75 = 75, EC90 = 90, EC99 = 99)
ec_check <- data.frame(
  level = names(ecx), paper = c(0.042, 0.126, 1.38),
  model = unname(ec50 * ecx / (100 - ecx))
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - paper) / paper)
stopifnot(all(abs(ec_check$pct_diff) < 1))
ec_check |>
  dplyr::rename("Level" = level, "Paper (ug/mL)" = paper, "Model (ug/mL)" = model, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

pd_curve <- typ_single |>
  filter(cohort %in% c("0.01 mg/kg IV", "0.1 mg/kg IV", "3 mg/kg IV"), time > 0)
ggplot(pd_curve, aes(conc_ug, mfi_a4b7)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ec_check$model, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)", y = "Free alpha4beta7 on CD4+ T cells (MFI)",
    title = "Replicates the Emax curve of Figure 5 of Li 2015",
    caption = "Dashed lines: EC75, EC90, EC99")
```

# Human projection

## Kd: Methods text versus Table 3

The Methods state that the human Kd was fixed at 0.031 nmol/L, the in vitro
EC50 on human primary T cells, while Table 3 lists Kd = 0.013 nmol/L
"not scaled". The Kd only matters at the lowest doses, where the target
binds almost all drug, so the 0.7 and 2.1 mg SC predictions of Table 4
discriminate. Only 0.031 nmol/L reproduces them, and that value is used in
`Li_2015_abrilumab_human`.

```{r kd-check}
sad_low <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~paper_cmax, ~paper_auc,
  0.7, 0.0009, 0.985,
  2.1, 0.004, 3.81
)
low_grid <- c(seq(0, 30, by = 0.05), seq(30.5, 600, by = 0.5))
sim_low <- function(kd) {
  ev <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sad_low)), function(i) {
    data.frame(id = i, dose = sad_low$dose[i],
      time = c(0, low_grid), amt = c(sad_low$dose[i], rep(0, length(low_grid))),
      evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(low_grid))), cmt = c("depot", rep("central", length(low_grid))))
  }))
  sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, events = ev, params = c(lkd = log(kd)), keep = "dose",
    returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10)) |>
    mutate(conc_ug = Cc * mw_factor)
  nca_interval(sim, "dose", filter(ev, evid == 1), start = 0, end = Inf) |>
    transmute(dose = grp, cmax, auc = aucinf.obs, kd = kd)
}
kd_cmp <- bind_rows(sim_low(0.031), sim_low(0.013)) |>
  left_join(sad_low, by = "dose") |>
  mutate(auc_pct_diff = 100 * (auc - paper_auc) / paper_auc)
kd_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg SC)" = dose, "Kd (nmol/L)" = kd, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "Paper Cmax" = paper_cmax, "AUC0-inf (h*ug/mL)" = auc, "Paper AUC" = paper_auc,
    "AUC % diff" = auc_pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(kd_cmp$auc_pct_diff[kd_cmp$kd == 0.031]) < 5),
  all(kd_cmp$auc_pct_diff[kd_cmp$kd == 0.013] < -40)
)
```

## Single and multiple dose profiles (Figure 6)

```{r human-sims}
sad <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~dose, ~cmt,
  "0.7 mg SC", 0.7, "depot",
  "2.1 mg SC", 2.1, "depot",
  "7 mg SC", 7, "depot",
  "21 mg SC", 21, "depot",
  "70 mg SC", 70, "depot",
  "210 mg SC", 210, "depot",
  "70 mg IV", 70, "central",
  "210 mg IV", 210, "central",
  "420 mg IV", 420, "central"
)
mad <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~dose,
  "7 mg SC Q4W x 3", 7,
  "21 mg SC Q4W x 3", 21,
  "70 mg SC Q4W x 3", 70,
  "210 mg SC Q4W x 3", 210
)
sad_grid <- c(seq(0, 30, by = 0.05), seq(30.5, 600, by = 0.5))
ev_sad <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sad)), function(i) {
  data.frame(id = i, regimen = sad$regimen[i],
    time = c(0, sad_grid), amt = c(sad$dose[i], rep(0, length(sad_grid))),
    evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(sad_grid))), cmt = c(sad$cmt[i], rep("central", length(sad_grid))))
}))
mad_grid <- c(seq(0, 84, by = 0.05), seq(84.5, 400, by = 0.5))
ev_mad <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(mad)), function(i) {
  data.frame(id = 100 + i, regimen = mad$regimen[i],
    time = c(0, 28, 56, mad_grid), amt = c(rep(mad$dose[i], 3), rep(0, length(mad_grid))),
    evid = c(rep(1L, 3), rep(0L, length(mad_grid))),
    cmt = c(rep("depot", 3), rep("central", length(mad_grid))))
}))
sim_human <- function(ev) {
  # The human projection has no omega; rxode2 warns for any multi-subject solve.
  suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human, events = ev, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame",
    atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10)) |>
    mutate(conc_ug = Cc * mw_factor)
}
hum_sad <- sim_human(ev_sad)
hum_mad <- sim_human(ev_mad)

ec_lines <- data.frame(level = c("EC50", "EC75", "EC90", "EC99"), conc = c(0.014, 0.042, 0.126, 1.38))
ggplot(hum_sad |> filter(time > 0, time <= 252, conc_ug >= 1e-4), aes(time, conc_ug, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.126, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 6A of Li 2015", caption = "Dashed line: EC90 = 0.126 ug/mL")

ggplot(hum_mad |> filter(time > 0, time <= 392, conc_ug >= 1e-4), aes(time, conc_ug, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(data = ec_lines, aes(yintercept = conc), colour = "grey40", linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time post first dose (days)", y = "Abrilumab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 6B of Li 2015", caption = "Dotted lines: EC50, EC75, EC90, EC99")
```

The text states that 21, 70, 210 and 420 mg cover EC90 for about 2, 3, 5 and
6 months, and that the four Q4W x 3 regimens stay above EC90 for 3-8 months.

```{r human-ec90}
dur_ec90 <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(regimen) |>
    summarise(months_above_ec90 = max(c(0, time[conc_ug >= 0.126])) / 30.4, .groups = "drop")
}
bind_rows(dur_ec90(hum_sad), dur_ec90(hum_mad)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Months above EC90 (from first dose)" = months_above_ec90) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## PKNCA against Table 4

Table 4 lists the predicted Cmax and AUC0-inf for the single-dose regimens,
and Cmax and an "AUCtau" after the third dose for the Q4W x 3 regimens. Its
footnote defines AUCtau as the AUC within the third dosing interval, but the
printed values are the AUC from the third dose (day 56) to infinity: the
day 56-84 AUC is 16-43% lower, while the day 56-infinity AUC matches all four
rows to 0.1%. The comparison below therefore uses the AUC from day 56 to
infinity. NCA is run with PKNCA on the free concentration in ug/mL, with time
in hours so the AUC units match Table 4.

```{r human-nca}
nca_sad_conc <- hum_sad |>
  transmute(id, regimen, time_h = time * 24, conc = conc_ug)
nca_sad_dose <- sad |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), time_h = 0) |>
  select(id, regimen, time_h, dose)
o_conc_sad <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_sad_conc, conc ~ time_h | regimen + id)
o_dose_sad <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_sad_dose, dose ~ time_h | regimen + id)
o_data_sad <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc_sad, o_dose_sad,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE))
nca_sad <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data_sad)

nca_mad_conc <- hum_mad |>
  transmute(id, regimen, time_h = time * 24, conc = conc_ug)
nca_mad_dose <- ev_mad |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  transmute(id, regimen, time_h = time * 24, dose = amt)
o_conc_mad <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_mad_conc, conc ~ time_h | regimen + id)
o_dose_mad <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_mad_dose, dose ~ time_h | regimen + id)
o_data_mad <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc_mad, o_dose_mad,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 56 * 24, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE))
nca_mad <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data_mad)

published_sad <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "0.7 mg SC", 0.0009, 0.985,
  "2.1 mg SC", 0.004, 3.81,
  "7 mg SC", 0.604, 186,
  "21 mg SC", 3.48, 1940,
  "70 mg SC", 13.5, 9500,
  "210 mg SC", 42.4, 32300,
  "70 mg IV", 22.7, 9520,
  "210 mg IV", 70.8, 32300,
  "420 mg IV", 143, 67000
)
published_mad <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "7 mg SC Q4W x 3", 1.69, 782,
  "21 mg SC Q4W x 3", 6.29, 4120,
  "70 mg SC Q4W x 3", 22.4, 17100,
  "210 mg SC Q4W x 3", 68.4, 55300
)
cmp_sad <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sad, reference = published_sad, by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp_mad <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mad, reference = published_mad, by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL"), tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp_table4 <- bind_rows(cmp_sad, cmp_mad)
cmp_table4 |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4,
  caption = "Typical-value human prediction vs Li 2015 Table 4 (single doses: Cmax and AUC0-inf; Q4W x 3: Cmax and AUC from the third dose on day 56 to infinity). * marks rows differing by >20%.")
```

```{r human-nca-assert}
pct <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9eE.+-]", "", cmp_table4[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(
  # A wrong Kd, molecular weight, volume or bioavailability moves these by
  # tens of percent; the typical-value solve is deterministic.
  abs(median(pct)) < 3,
  all(abs(pct) < 15)
)
```

All `r nrow(cmp_table4)` Table 4 values are reproduced within
`r round(max(abs(pct)), 1)`%. The largest differences are the Cmax values of
the two lowest SC doses, which Table 4 prints with one significant digit.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Human Kd.** Table 3 lists Kd = 0.013 nmol/L ("not scaled") while the
  Methods fix the human Kd at 0.031 nmol/L, the human in vitro EC50. The
  human model uses 0.031 nmol/L because only that value reproduces the
  paper's own Table 4 predictions at 0.7 and 2.1 mg SC (section "Kd" above);
  0.013 nmol/L under-predicts their AUC by more than half. The Table 3 entry
  is taken to be a transcription error (0.013 is the monkey value).
* **Observed quantity.** Both models report the free concentration Cf. The
  Methods fit molar concentration data "with the free AMG 181 concentration
  (Cf) calculated using the equation shown in Figure 1", and Table 4 is
  reproduced only by Cf (total drug at 0.7 mg SC would give a Cmax of about
  0.2 ug/mL, not 0.0009 ug/mL). The PD model is driven by the same
  concentration converted to ug/mL.
* **Constant total receptor.** Figure 1 draws receptor synthesis (ksyn) and
  degradation (kdeg), but Table 2 reports only Rtot and Kint and no kdeg.
  The model therefore uses the constant-Rtot form of the QE approximation
  (receptor degradation equal to complex internalization), in which bound
  drug is `Ctot - Cf = Rtot * Cf / (Kd + Cf)` and is eliminated at Kint.
  This form reproduces Table 4.
* **Distribution of free drug only.** Linear elimination (CL) and transfer
  to the peripheral compartment (K12) act on free drug, the standard QE-TMDD
  form; the paper does not print the differential equations.
* **Table 4 multiple-dose AUC.** The Table 4 footnote calls the Q4W x 3
  AUC "AUCtau: AUC within the 3rd dosing interval", but the printed values
  equal the AUC from the third dose to infinity (see "PKNCA against
  Table 4"); the exposure ratios in Table 4 were computed from those values.
* **Units and molecular weight.** Doses are in mg and drug amounts in mg;
  the molar conversion uses the "~144 kD" molecular weight from the Methods.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 gives IIV as percentages without a definition. They
  are read as CV% of a log-normal eta, omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). If the
  authors reported sqrt(omega^2) x 100 instead, the Rtot variance would be
  3.24 rather than 1.44; the CL and Vc variances would change by less than
  10%. The CL-Vc correlation 0.642 is converted to a covariance.
* **Residual error.** "A mixture of proportional plus additive" error is
  encoded as `add(addSd) + prop(propSd)` with the Table 2 values (20.1% and
  1.11 nmol/L), on the free concentration.
* **PD model.** Emax, E0 and EC50 were fitted to Study A only, with no IIV
  or residual error reported; `mfi_a4b7` is therefore an algebraic output
  without an error model. The paper reports the EC50 as
  0.0140 +/- 0.0082 ug/mL (estimate +/- standard error). The human projection
  uses the monkey EC values only as reference concentrations, so the human
  model carries no PD output.
* **Human projection.** All human parameters are fixed typical values; the
  model has no IIV and a zero residual error, as the paper simulated typical
  profiles only.
* **Monkey weight.** The monkey model has no weight covariate. The figures
  above use the median weight of 2.8 kg to convert mg/kg doses to mg; the
  toxicology-study animals were heavier on average (mean 3.43 kg).
* **Study A IV dose levels.** Table 1 lists the Study A IV doses as 0.01,
  0.1, 0.3 and 3 mg/kg, while the Figure 2A legend shows 0.01, 0.1, 1 and
  3 mg/kg IV. The Figure 2A replication above follows the figure legend.
* **Low-dose monkey cohort.** The paper notes that the model under-predicts
  the 0.01 mg/kg IV cohort; that misfit is part of the published model.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article (PubMed,
  checked 2026-11-24).
